questions.q: In the lab's flow, what keeps the automation from firing on catalog requests for unrelated items like a laptop or a monitor?
options: Nothing — the flow fires on every Requested Item created, regardless of item
The Service Catalog trigger's condition filters on cat_item equal to "New Software License Request"
A separate ACL blocks the flow from running on other items
The flow only runs if a developer manually starts it
questions.explain: The cat_item filter on the trigger condition scopes the flow to exactly one catalog item.

questions.q: What does the lab's If/Else step actually compare to decide the approval path?
options: The requester's job title
The Software Name variable
The License Cost variable, read as a data pill, compared against 500
The number of items in the requester's cart
questions.explain: License Cost is read off the Requested Item as a pill, then compared against the $500 threshold with an If/Else.

questions.q: For a license costing $500 or more, what happens if Manager approval is rejected?
options: Finance approval runs anyway, regardless of Manager's decision
The flow skips Finance entirely and routes straight into the shared rejection path
The request is automatically approved by default
The flow pauses indefinitely waiting for a human to intervene
questions.explain: The second If/Else checks Manager's outcome first; only an approved result continues on to the Finance Approval action.

questions.q: Why does the lab route both the under-$500 branch's rejection and the $500-plus branch's rejection into one shared rejection path instead of two separate ones?
options: Flow Designer technically forbids more than one rejection path per flow
Both branches need different wording, so sharing a path is actually impossible
One shared path avoids duplicating the same notification and close-out logic across every branch that can end in rejection
Shared paths are required for the flow to save correctly
questions.explain: Reusing one rejection sequence avoids building near-identical notification-and-close logic twice.

questions.q: What does the lab's fulfillment step actually do once every required approval stage has cleared?
options: It creates an entirely new catalog item for next time
It emails the Finance team a summary report
An Update Record action marks the Requested Item as fulfilled, and a notification confirms the license is ready
It restarts the flow from the trigger to double-check the approval
questions.explain: Fulfillment closes the loop on the Requested Item's record and lets the requester know the outcome.
